From the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise, Rc. Letter No.P&E 2(4)/1191/2020, dated 12.02.2020.

ORDER:-

The Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise in his letter read above has stated that the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India have notified the Food Safety and Standards (Alcoholic Beverages) Regulation, 2018 on the standards specified for distilled and un-distilled alcoholic beverages with effect from 01.04.2019.

2. The Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise has also stated that under the para 5.12 of the Food Safety and Standards (Alcoholic Beverages) Regulation, 2018, there shall be a statutory warning printed in English Language or in their local or regional language without repeating the English version and the size of statutory warning shall not be less than 3 mm as mentioned below: -

“CONSUMPTION OF ALCOHOL IS INJURIOUS TO HEALTH” “BE SAFE - DONT DRINK AND DRIVE”

3. Further, the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise has stated that the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India have insisted to keep the text of statutory warning in the square box uniform across the country as stipulated under Para 5.12 of the Food Safety and Standards (Alcoholic Beverages) Regulation, 2018 as mentioned below :-

“CONSUMPTION OF ALCOHOL IS INJURIOUS TO HEALTH “BE SAFE - DONT DRINK AND DRIVE”

(p.t.o.)

—

4. The Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise has, therefore, requested the Government to issue the following amendment to Rule 25(I) of the Tamil Nadu Liquor (Licence and Permit) Rules, 1981, so as to ensure that the rules are in conformity with the standards given by Food Safety and Standards Authority of India.

5. Accordingly, the following Notification shall be published in the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette: -

The chronology of events that contributed to unauthorised occupation of Government land and short collection of lease rent are discussed below:

Despite clear instructions (June 1993) by GoTN to take back the five acres of land adjoining the leased land, the Revenue Officers entertained a request (January 1994) from the School to lease out this parcel of five acres as well. Based on recommendations from District Revenue authorities, the Commissioner of Land Administration (CLA) recommended (October 1998) to Government for leasing of an additional two acres, out of the additional five acres requested by the School. Even as this proposal was under examination by GoTN, the School management requested (June 1999) GoTN to sell the entire land to them on a concessional rate. Acting on this request, GoTN directed (August 1999) CLA to furnish a report on the request made by the School.
